kings1.4.p1.b1.text: So King Solomon ruled over Israel,

kings1.4.p1.b2.text: and these were his chief officials: Azariah son of Zadok was the priest;

kings1.4.p1.b3.text: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the army …

kings1.4.p1.b4.text: … and Adoniram son of Abda was in charge of the forced labor.

kings1.4.p2.b1.text: Solomon had twelve governors over all Israel to provide food for the king and his household. Each one would arrange provisions for one month of the year,

kings1.4.p2.b2.text: Ben-abinadab in Naphath-dor (Taphath, a daughter of Solomon, was his wife);

kings1.4.p2.b3.text: … the region of Argob in Bashan with its sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars …

kings1.4.p3.b1.text: The people of Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore, and they were eating and drinking and rejoicing.

kings1.4.p3.b2.text: And Solomon reigned over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt.

kings1.4.p3.b3.text: Solomon’s provisions for a single day were thirty cors of fine flour, sixty cors of meal, ten fat oxen, twenty range oxen, and a hundred sheep, as well as deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened poultry.

kings1.4.p3.b4.text: … and he had peace on all sides.

kings1.4.p4.b1.text: Throughout the days of Solomon, Judah and Israel dwelt securely from Dan to Beersheba, each man under his own vine and his own fig tree.

kings1.4.p4.b2.text: Solomon had 4,000 stalls for his chariot horses and 12,000 horses.

kings1.4.p5.b1.text: And God gave Solomon wisdom, exceedingly deep insight, and understanding beyond measure, like the sand on the seashore.

kings1.4.p5.b2.text: … from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop growing in the wall …

kings1.4.p5.b3.text: Solomon composed three thousand proverbs, and his songs numbered a thousand and five.

kings1.4.p5.b4.text: So men of all nations came to listen to Solomon’s wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth, who had heard of his wisdom.
